projects.title: Soucou 3.5
projects.description: A video game where the progression involves searching for keys in a basement, leading to a final battle that requires dodging and deflecting projectiles.

creationProcess.description: Design: The game was designed by defining the necessary components, including various levels, a shop, towers, enemies, a path, and several menus. A variety of towers and enemies were designed to create a linear progression. Game Engine/Tower Defense Library Creation: Godot was chosen as the software to build the tower defense game engine. The system was designed to be configurable, making it easy to create new towers, levels, and enemies, and to assign graphical elements such as textures. Asset Creation: Game graphics—including textures for towers, enemies, and menus—were created using Pixelorama. The environment utilizes textures reused from a personal project of ours (a mod for the game *Mindustry*). Menu graphics were created in Figma and exported. Assembly: The graphics and design concepts were assembled within the game engine to build the game, applying the correct textures, names, and data for towers, maps, and enemies. Balancing and Testing: We then tested the game to ensure proper progression. Adjustments were made to variables such as player income, tower costs, and enemy health to improve the overall gameplay experience. Publication: Finally, the game was published on a website—in our case, hosted on GitHub Pages.
